current.name: 3i Infrastructure plc
current.growthThesis: 3i Infrastructure is an economic-infrastructure capital allocator whose screen profile is income-and-cheapness, not growth: earnings are down sharply (−77%), Piotroski is weak (2), and ROE is only mid-single digits. Positive FCF, low gearing, and a ~3.5% yield support a hold-style value case near book, but that is NAV/distribution compounding rather than a distinguishable operating growth edge over a multi-year horizon. The value-screen hold and family passes (cheapness, dividend) are evidence of relative value, not a reason to upgrade the growth stance.
growthDrivers: Inflation-linked and contracted cash flows in economic infrastructure assets can support NAV and distributions over time
Low balance-sheet gearing (D/E ~14%) leaves room to fund bolt-on investments without stressed leverage
Positive free cash flow on the screen supports the dividend and reinvestment capacity
growthConstraints: Screen earnings growth deeply negative (−77%), so near-term growth optics are poor
Weak Piotroski (2) and only 8% ROE undermine a quality-compounder story
Value-screen signal is hold with few quality/GARP models passing
current.valuationNote: P/E ~12 and P/B ~1.0 with a ~3.5% yield look fair for an infrastructure allocator, but collapsing earnings make the multiple less supportive of a growth-led return case.
current.expectedReturnBand: low-to-mid single-digit annualised over 5 years if distributions and NAV hold near book; not a growth-compounding setup on current screen evidence
keyRisks: Further earnings or valuation write-downs in the infrastructure portfolio
Interest-rate or discount-rate moves compressing asset values and exit multiples
Dividend pressure if FCF or underlying distributions weaken
Thin fundamental quality (Piotroski 2) may signal deteriorating portfolio health
whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence of sustained earnings recovery and rising ROE on a later screen vintage
Clear acceleration in NAV/FCF with quality metrics (e.g. Piotroski) improving
A durable growth driver in the portfolio mix (e.g. energy-transition or digital infra) showing through on the card
openQuestions: How much of the earnings drop is mark-to-market versus cash generation?
Is the screen vehicle label 'operating' masking an investment-company NAV model?
What is the mix of regulated vs demand-risk assets behind the FCF?
current.freeNotes: First name in a fresh walk (0 assessed). No lessons or network links to apply. Screen flags hold and negative earnings growth; stance deliberately diverges from any temptation to treat cheapness/dividend family passes as a growth upgrade. Treated as capital allocator into economic infrastructure rather than a classic operating compounder despite vehicle=operating on the card.

lessons.title: Cheapness plus shrinking earnings is not growth
lessons.statement: When a constituent passes value cheapness or dividend families but shows sharply negative earnings growth and a weak Piotroski score, treat the screen as a value/income signal only. Do not upgrade the growth stance without separate evidence of earnings or NAV compounding recovery.
